recommendations: Open and structure the visit: briefly introduce yourself and role, outline session goals, and review confidentiality and its limits (harm to self/others, abuse, court orders).

Use reflective summaries and ‘chunk-and-check’: periodically reflect key points (e.g., social withdrawal, 1-year course, worsening in 6 months) and ask if you’re understanding correctly to build rapport and accuracy.

Systematically assess DSM-5-TR for GAD and rule-outs: ask about uncontrollability of worry; associated symptoms (restlessness, fatigue, concentration, irritability, muscle tension, sleep), functional impairment, substances (caffeine/alcohol), medical causes (thyroid), and screen for panic, OCD, PTSD, social anxiety, and depression; consider brief tools (GAD-7) and safety assessment.
